leakage.confidence_note: Source uses only ctx.history/ctx.session/ctx.position with an ctx.actionable gate and no reference to scoring, dataset, split, or seed; I cannot verify from source alone that history[-1] is guaranteed to be a closed bar rather than a forming bar, but nothing in the code attempts to reach beyond the per-bar view.

statistics.confidence_note: The metric is supported by 384 sessions / 243 downside / 466 trades on train and 86 / 54 / 106 on validation (not degenerate); p=0.0885 is far above the resolution floor (1e-4) and the gate's null_max_mean (0.147) is consistent with the deflation expected_max (0.134) given null_moments mean=-0.003, sd=0.075 over 20 trials; the apparent disagreement between the deflation 'clears_selection_bar: true' and the gate 'REJECT' is explicitly explained in the notes as a margin vs. a p-value from different null constructions, not an unexplained inconsistency. What I cannot see is what n_nulls=17 versus trials=20 means for the gate's null construction, whether the train-side skew=4.23 / kurtosis=36.3 concentrates the numerator in a few sessions (only validation concentration is shown, best_session_share=0.084, top5% share=0.31), and the interpretation scale for null_reference_divergence on validation (trades_per_session=0.0283).

economics.confidence_note: The fill model's spread field is null so I cannot confirm the entry/exit prices account for realistic slippage on NQ, but the per-trade edge is ~8.6 index points (~34 ticks) versus a 0.2-point round-trip commission, giving wide margin to absorb fill degradation; the docstring's developed hypothesis (continuation of outsized, high-volume, trend-aligned bars) is one arm of the pre-registered 'continue vs. give-back' question and is a legitimate narrowing, and the code implements it directly (range outlier vs. session median, volume filter, session-open trend filter, two-bar confirmation, then continuation entry). Trade count 466/384 sessions, ~3.1-hour average holding, commission 2.3% of gross, and out-of-sample score degradation of only 0.048 all argue the result is not an artifact of inactivity or cost absorption.

reasons: Breadth is genuinely broad on train: 12/18 months positive (66.7%), 5/6 weekdays positive (83.3%), 15/24 hours positive (62.5%) — no minority of periods is holding up the total.
Best-session share is 7.9% on train and 8.4% on validation; removing the best session cannot flip the sign of the total, so there is no single-session dependence.
Validation breadth mirrors train breadth (4/5 months positive, 4/6 weekdays positive, ~14/23 hours positive), so the out-of-sample look does not reveal a collapse to a narrow regime.

The largest month (2025-04, ~1462) plus the next two together are ~71% of train PnL, and top-5% profit concentration is 44.3% on train / 31.0% on validation — this is context, not grounds for a veto under the measured correlation between concentration and validation, and the result remains positive if the best month is removed.
The rule fires 466 times over 281/384 exposed sessions in train and 106 times in validation, so this is not a rule that only fires a few times.
robustness.confidence_note: I was not given the strategy's parameters or rule text, so I cannot rule out suspiciously specific parameter values or many small filters fitted to the sample.
